login.title: Sign in
login.lede: Sign in with the email and password the owner gave you.

home.lede: This is where every rupee sits right now. Add an entry whenever money moves.
home.ledeSupervisor: Record what you spend at the site, and count your cash at the end of the day.
home.emptyHint: Start in Setup: add your firms, sites, parties, clients and bank accounts. Then add your first entry.
home.emptySupervisor: Nothing here yet. When the office gives you cash, it shows up here.

masters.readOnly: Only the owner can change these.
masters.lede: The lists the forms pick from: firms, sites, parties and clients, contracts, bank or cash accounts, materials and GST rates.

delete.title: Delete (testing only)
delete.warning: Only while the app is being built. Deleting is permanent. Anything that entries, work orders, bank accounts or staff logins still use cannot be deleted — switch it off instead.
delete.inUse: Can’t delete: it is still used by {what}. Switch it off instead.

history.title: Change log

errors.not_allowed: You are not allowed to do this.
errors.inactive: This account is switched off. Ask the owner.
errors.cash_matches: The cash matches the books exactly. Nothing to record — well done!
errors.other_firm: This belongs to the other firm. Switch firm at the top right first.
errors.duplicate_bill: This bill number is already in the books for this party. Cancel that entry first if it was wrong
errors.bank_needs_firm: A bank account belongs to one firm. Choose it.

errors.item_rate: Type the rate for one unit, e.g. 350 or 1,250.50.
errors.invalid_gstin: A GST number has 15 characters, like 27AAAAA0000A1Z5. Check it against the paper.
errors.method_account: Online and cheque come from a bank account. Cash comes from a cash account.
errors.cash_needs_firm: Each firm keeps its own cash. Choose the firm.

plain.excess: Extra cash found at day close

money.title: Money we hold
money.hint: Bank accounts and cash in hand.

betweenFirms.title: Between our firms
betweenFirms.hint: When one firm’s money paid for another firm.

heldByClients.title: Held by clients
heldByClients.hint: Still our money. It comes back later.

gst.title: GST
gst.hint: GST paid on party bills, to claim back, and GST charged on client bills, to pay.

owner.title: Owner
owner.hint: The owner’s own money, old balances and cash differences.

sites.title: Sites
sites.hint: Profit = billed to the client − all costs, from every firm.

tds.title: TDS
tds.hint: TDS deducted from party bills, to pay to the government.

new.title: What happened?
new.lede: Pick what happened. You fill in a short form; the app does the accounting.

entries.cancelHint: Nothing is deleted. The app adds an exact opposite entry, so the history stays.

daybook.lede: Everything typed into the app, newest first. Tap a serial number to see what it changed.
daybook.firmLede: What this firm’s books show right now, and every entry in them.
daybook.siteLede: What this site has billed and spent, and every entry for it.
daybook.sitesHintFirm: Only this firm’s share. Profit = billed − costs.
daybook.costsHint: Costs at this site, by kind of work.

vendor-bill.title: Bill from a party
vendor-bill.when: A party sent a bill for material, machines or work.
vendor-bill.what: The site’s cost goes up by the bill before GST. The GST is kept apart: the firm claims it back. If TDS is deducted, it is kept apart too: it is owed to the government, so the party is paid less. The firm owes the party the total less TDS, even before anyone pays. Paying it later is a separate entry: “Pay a party”.

hints.firm_id: The firm named on the bill.
hints.vendor_id: Not in the list? Add them in Setup → Parties.
hints.site_id: Where the material or work was used.
hints.bill_no: The number printed on the party’s bill.
hints.narration: Anything worth remembering, e.g. “40 bags cement”.
hints.cost_head: Left empty, the bill counts as material.
hints.tds_rate: Left empty, no TDS is deducted. The rate is worked out on the bill before GST.

pay-vendor.title: Pay a party
pay-vendor.when: Money went to a party by bank, UPI or cash.
pay-vendor.what: What the firm owes the party goes down, and the bank or cash goes down by the same amount. The site’s cost does not change: it was counted when the bill came. If one firm’s bank pays another firm’s bill, the app notes that the second firm now owes the first.

hints.firm_id: The firm whose bill this pays.
hints.from_account_id: The bank or cash the money left from.
hints.reference: Optional. Fill it in when you have it: it helps match the bank statement later.
hints.payment_method: Online or cheque: the firm’s bank. Cash: the firm’s cash.

client-bill.title: Bill to a client
client-bill.when: We sent a client a bill for work done.
client-bill.what: The work done (the bill before GST) counts as the site’s income. The GST on top is owed to the government. The client owes us the total after TDS, retention and security deposit; those are still our money, just held for now.

hints.work_order_id: The contract this bill is for.
hints.retention: Leave empty to use the work order’s retention %, worked out on the bill before GST.
hints.security_deposit: Leave empty to use the work order’s security deposit %, worked out on the bill before GST.
hints.tds_rate: Left empty, the work order’s TDS % is used. Pick 0% if the client deducts none. Worked out on the bill before GST.

client-receipt.title: Money from a client
client-receipt.what: Money in the bank goes up, and what the client owes us goes down. Profit does not change: it was earned when the work was billed.

hints.reference: Optional. Fill it in when you have it: it helps match the bank statement later.
hints.payment_method: Online or cheque: the firm’s bank. Cash: the firm’s cash.

site-spend.title: Spent at a site
site-spend.when: Cash was spent at a site: labour, small material, diesel, tea…
site-spend.what: The site’s cost goes up and the cash in hand goes down by the same amount.

hints.narration: What was bought or paid for, e.g. “12 helpers, 1 day”.
hints.paid_to_id: Pick the person or shop if they are in the list.
hints.material_id: If you bought a material (cement, sand…), pick it here. The type then fills in by itself.

day-close.title: Count the cash
day-close.when: At the end of the day, count the cash in hand.
day-close.what: The app knows how much cash there should be. If what you count is different, the difference is recorded as cash short (or extra) and shows on the owner’s screen. It is never hidden inside another cost.

hints.counted: Exactly what is in hand now. Can be 0.

owner-money.title: Owner’s money
owner-money.when: The owner put personal money into the business, or took some out.
owner-money.what: Money the owner puts in is not income, and money taken out is not a site cost. Both are recorded as the owner’s own money, so site profits stay true.

opening.title: Starting balance
opening.why: A balance carried over from the old Excel records, so the app starts where the books left off.

vendor_bill.title: Bill from a party
vendor_bill.why: The firm owes the money from the moment the bill arrives, even before paying. The cost, before GST, belongs to the site where it was used; the GST on it is claimed back, so it is not a cost. TDS deducted is owed to the government, so the party is paid less, and it is kept in the TDS record.

vendor_payment.title: Paid a party
vendor_payment.why: Paying a bill does not change the site’s cost; it was counted when the bill came. Money just moves from our bank or cash to the party.

site_cash_expense.title: Spent at a site
site_cash_expense.why: This is real spending, so it goes onto the site’s cost. The cash in hand goes down by the same amount.

client_bill.title: Bill to a client
client_bill.why: The value of the work, before GST, is income; the GST on top is collected for the government. TDS, retention and security deposit are still our money, just held by others: TDS is claimed back in the tax return, retention comes back after the defect period.

client_receipt.title: Money from a client
client_receipt.why: Being paid does not change profit. It turns “the client owes us” into money in the bank.

cash_transfer.title: Money moved
cash_transfer.why: Moving money between our own pockets is not spending. The total stays the same.

cash_close_difference.title: Cash short or extra
cash_close_difference.why: The counted cash did not match the books. The difference is recorded on its own, never slipped into another cost.

owner_capital.title: Owner put money in
owner_capital.why: Every rupee has to come from somewhere. Here it comes from the owner, so it is recorded as the owner’s money in the business.

owner_drawing.title: Owner took money out
owner_drawing.why: Recorded as the owner’s own money going out, so it never looks like a site cost.

reversal.title: Cancelling entry
reversal.why: The exact opposite of an earlier entry, so the two add up to nothing. Nothing is ever deleted: the history stays.

sheet.title: Many entries at once
sheet.lede: One row is one entry. Tab moves to the next box, Enter to the row below. You can paste rows copied from Excel. Nothing is saved until you press Save, and every row gets the same checks as the form.
sheet.empty: Fill in at least one row first.
sheet.fromNew: Many entries at once? Type them in a sheet

party.indexLede: Every party this firm owes money to, just like the outstanding sheet.
party.name: Party name
party.empty: No parties for this firm yet. Open a party below and add its first bill.
party.openOtherHint: Pick it to add its first bill or payment. A brand-new party?
party.noFirm: No firm is set up yet. Add one in Setup.
party.billsHint: The opening balance comes first, then every bill from this party.
party.noBills: No bills yet. The opening balance and every new bill will show here.
party.noPayments: No payments yet. Money paid to this party will show here.
party.addHint: Type in the rows like Excel: Tab and Enter move between boxes, and you can paste rows copied from Excel. Then press Save.
party.searchHint: Type a name to find a party…
party.clickHint: Click any row to open that party.
party.needSite: Add your sites first: every bill needs the site it was for.
party.needAccount: Add this firm's bank and cash accounts first: every payment needs where the money came from.
party.noMaterials: Your materials list is empty. Add cement, sand, steel and the rest once, and they show up here on every bill.

dashboard.title: {firm} – Dashboard
dashboard.lede: How much this firm owes its parties, and how much is paid.
dashboard.chart: Each party: paid out of total
dashboard.chartHint: Bar length is what we owed in all. Green is paid, red is still to pay.

client.indexLede: Every client who owes this firm money: bills given and money received.
client.name: Client name
client.searchHint: Type a name to find a client…
client.clickHint: Click any row to open that client.
client.empty: No client bills or receipts for this firm yet. Open a client below and add their first bill.
client.openOtherHint: Pick them to add their first bill or receipt. A brand-new client?
client.billsHint: The opening due comes first, then running and stage bills given to this client. The client cuts TDS, retention and deposit; the rest is what they owe.
client.receiptsHint: Payments that came in from this client.
client.addBillsHint: Add each item with its GST. Leave TDS, retention or deposit empty if the client cut none. Then press Save.

quick.nothingOwed: Nothing is due to {name} right now.

firm.switchLabel: Working in {firm}. Tap to switch firm.
firm.switchFailed: Could not switch firm. Try again.
firm.commonHint: Owner or supervisor cash: belongs to no firm.

stock.title: Stock
stock.lede: Stock at each site, whichever firm bought it. Everything bought on a party’s bill comes in by itself; what supervisors report used on the daily report goes out. Cancel a bill and it comes out again.
stock.belowZero: More was reported used than bought here. A party bill may not be entered yet.
stock.none: Nothing bought yet. Add a party bill with its items and it shows here.

report.title: Daily report
report.lede: One site, one day: the work done, the material used, labour and staff, other costs, and what the day made. Supervisors fill it for their sites.
report.materialNote: Comes out of this site’s stock, at the average rate it was bought at
report.noSites: No sites given to you yet. Ask the office to add you to a site in People.
report.noWork: No work entered for this day yet. Add it below.
report.lines: {n, plural, =0 {Nothing entered yet} one {# line} other {# lines}}

use.addHint: Pick the material and type how much was used. Its unit, rate and amount fill in by themselves, with what will be left at this site. Red means more than the stock shows: a party bill may not be entered yet.
use.belowZero: More than this site’s stock. A party bill may not be entered yet.

work.addHint: One block per activity. Write what was done, pick the unit and type the rate. The measurement boxes follow the unit: M3 asks length × width × height, M2 length × width, Nos just the quantity. Use No. for how many alike (two walls: No. 2).
work.unitFirst: Pick the unit first. The measurement boxes appear for it.

report.noneUsed: No material entered for this day yet. Add it below.

errors.bad_quantity: Type the quantity, a number above zero like 0.45 or 483.
errors.need_measurement: This has no measurement. Type at least one, or remove it.
errors.bad_count: No. must be a number above zero, or left empty for 1.
errors.bad_length: Type the length, a number above zero like 4.3.
errors.bad_width: Type the width, a number above zero like 0.45.
errors.bad_height: Type the height, a number above zero like 2.8.
errors.bad_rate: The rate is not a rupee amount, like 600 or 2,500.
errors.not_removed: That line could not be removed. Supervisors can remove only their own lines, on the day they added them.
errors.already_marked: Someone here is already marked for this day, or present at another site. Open the day again to see who is left.
errors.need_description: Write what the cost was, like Tractor.
errors.pick_head: Pick what the cost was for.
errors.bad_ot: Type OT hours as a number from 0 to 16, like 2 or 1.5.
errors.ot_absent: OT can only be given on a day the person was present.
errors.no_rate: This person has no rate in Setup → Workers and staff. Add it there first.

report.costNote: Material, labour, staff and other costs
report.profitNote: Work done less the day’s costs
report.labourNote: {p} present · {a} absent. A day is 8 hours; OT is paid per hour on top
report.noLabour: Nobody marked for this day yet. Mark who came below.
report.noWorkers: No workers or staff on the list for this site yet.
report.allMarked: Everyone on the list is marked for this day.
report.workerList: Add them in Setup → Workers and staff
report.otherNote: Tractor, labour colony, room, light, petrol: anything else the site cost today

labour.addHint: Tap P (present) or A (absent) for each person, and type OT hours worked past the 8-hour day. The pay comes from the rate in Setup: a worker’s day is 8 hours at their hourly rate; staff get their day rate. Each OT hour pays a day ÷ 8. Anyone not marked is not saved.
labour.name: Name

other.addHint: Write what it was, pick what it was for, and type how many and the rate. Tractor is machine hire, not labour. Leave how many empty for 1.
other.head: What for

tds.title: TDS record
tds.lede: Every bill with TDS, with its rate, section and amount. TDS we deducted from parties is owed to the government. TDS clients deducted from our bills we can claim back.
tds.toClaim: TDS clients deducted, to claim back

salary.title: Salary
salary.lede: What each worker and staff member has earned, from the attendance marked on the daily reports at every site: days present at their day’s pay, plus OT hours. Open a name for their salary slip.
salary.none: No attendance marked in this period. Mark it on the Daily report.
salary.name: Name
salary.noDays: No days marked for this person in this period.
salary.forDays: {n, plural, one {# day present} other {# days present}}

ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.pick: Pick a vendor, client or site
ledger.hint: Pick a vendor, client or site to see every entry in date order, with the balance after each one.
ledger.notFound: That vendor, client or site is not in this firm’s list.

vendor.dr: {name} has been paid {amount} more than billed (advance).

search.more: {count} more: keep typing to narrow the list

form.noCashAccount: This firm has no cash account yet. Add one in Setup → Money accounts (kind: Owner cash, firm: this firm).
form.noBankAccount: This firm has no bank account yet. Add one in Setup → Money accounts.
